issues: Verification reserve can be consumed by worker startup. In Master._worker_result, editable-worker seconds is calculated as deadline - time.monotonic() - reserve before recovery preparation and two sequential subprocess.run configuration queries, each permitting 30 seconds. That stale duration is later passed to self.process, which calls self.remaining(seconds) without subtracting the reserve again. For example, with 100 seconds remaining, a 40-second reserve, and a nominal worker limit of at least 60 seconds, the worker receives a 60-second allowance. If preparation and queries consume 30 seconds, the worker can still run for 60 seconds, leaving only 10 seconds for supervisor verification. The fixed query timeouts can themselves exhaust a short remaining run budget. Repair by using an absolute editable-work cutoff of self.deadline - reserve, bounding each query by the remaining preparation/work allowance, and recalculating the worker allowance immediately before launch. Refuse launch once that cutoff is reached and refresh the reported budget to reflect actual availability. Add focused regression coverage for delayed configuration queries and an exhausted cutoff.
next_actions: Enforce the absolute editable-work cutoff across preparation, configuration inspection, and worker execution.
